articles.title: किमदेखि एलिनसम्म : विदेशीको भिसा, विवाह र गतिविधिको डरलाग्दो रिपोर्ट
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । विदेशी नागरिक नेपाल घुम्न, व्यापार गर्न वा अध्ययनका लागि आउने गरेका छन् । तर अध्यागमन र सुरक्षा निकायको अनुसन्धानले यसरी आउने केही विवाह, भाषा केन्द्र र एनजीओको आवरणमा धार्मिक प्रचारदेखि शंकास्पद गतिविधिसम्म गरेको देखाएको छ । पिटर क्वाङ सियोङ किमदेखि एलिन बिट ब्रोगस्ट्रोमसम्मका घटनाले राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामाथि गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएको छ ।

विदेशी नागरिक नेपाल किन आउँछन् ? यसको सामान्य जवाफ हा घुम्न, व्यापार गर्न, अध्ययन गर्न, व्यवसाय गर्न वा नेपालमा केही समय बस्न । तर अध्यागमन विभाग र सुरक्षा निकायको अनुसन्धानले केही विदेशीको नेपाल बसाइँको उद्देश्य सामान्यभन्दा निकै फरक र गम्भीर हुनसक्ने देखाएको छ । यसको एउटा उद्धाहरण हुन्, दक्षिण कोरियाली मूलका अमेरिकी नागरिक पिटर क्वाङ सियोङ किम । उनी विगत एक महिनादेखि अध्यागमन विभागको हिरासतमा थिए । तर सर्वोच्च अदालतले बन्दीप्रत्यक्षीकरण रिटमाथि फैसला गर्दै उनलाई थुनामुक्त गर्न आदेश दिएको छ ।

किम सन् २०१३ देखि नेपाल आउजाउ गर्दै आएका थिए । नेपाली महिला निलम बर्देवासँग विवाह गरेपछि उनले वैवाहिक भिसासमेत लिएका थिए । तर अध्यागमन विभागले उनलाई साउनमा एक वर्ष नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न नपाउने गरी देश निकाला गरेको थियो ।

त्यसविरुद्ध उनकी श्रीमतीले सर्वोच्चमा रिट दायर गरेकी थिइन् । किममाथिको अनुसन्धानमा भने उनको गतिविधि धार्मिक प्रचार, भिसाको दुरुपयोग र राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षासँग जोडिएको विषयमा केन्द्रित देखिन्छ । अनुसन्धान अनुसार किमले दोलखाको चरिकोटमा भाषा केन्द्र सञ्चालन गरेका थिए ।

सन् २०१८ मा भीमेश्वर बहिरा आधारभूत विद्यालयमा क्रिश्चियन धर्म प्रचार गरेको र तत्कालीन प्रधानाध्यापकलाई धर्म परिवर्तन गराएको आरोपसमेत अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ । काभ्रेको नमोबुद्धमा रहेको द लाइट एन्ड सल्ट स्कुलमार्फत् विपन्न बालबालिकालाई लक्षित गरेर धर्म प्रचार गरिएको दाबी पनि गरिएको छ ।

त्यस्तै दोलखा, सिन्धुली र काभ्रेमा धार्मिक गतिविधि विस्तार गर्ने, स्थानीय अवस्था र भविष्यमा लगानी गर्नुपर्ने क्षेत्रबारे रिपोर्ट तयार पारेर विदेशस्थित संस्थामा पठाउने गरेको अनुसन्धानमा भेटिएको बताइएको छ । यसका लागि उनले अमेरिकामा रहेका संस्थाहरुबाट आर्थिक सहयोग पाउने गरेका थिए ।

मिसनरी कार्यलाई निरन्तरता दिनकै लागि रणनीतिक रूपमा उनले व्यावसायिक भिसालाई विवाह भिसामा परिणत गर्ने योजना बनाएको देखिन्छ । उनको वैवाहिक सम्बन्ध नेपालमा दीर्घकालीन बसोवास गर्ने र आफ्नो कानुनी हैसियत जोगाउन मात्र प्रयोग भएको देखिन्छ ।

अनुसन्धानमा सन् २०२२ को नेपाल मिसन रिपोर्ट पनि फेला परेको बताइएको छ । बिजनेस भिसामा बस्दा उनले गरेको गतिविधि थाहा पाएर डिपोर्ट हुनसक्ने जोखिमका कारण वैवाहिक भिसा लिने योजना बनाइएको २०२२ नेपाल मिसन रिपोर्टमा उल्लेख भएको अध्यागमनको दाबी छ । किम ७२ वर्षका र उनकी नेपाली श्रीमती ३० वर्षकी रहेको तथा किमको अमेरिकामा समेत परिवार र सन्तान रहेको अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ ।

किमजस्तै अरु को को ?

तर यस्तो विषय किममा मात्रै सीमित छैन । स्वीडेनी नागरिक एलिन बिट ब्रोगस्ट्रोमको विषय पनि अनुसन्धानमा आएको छ । ५१ वर्षीया एलिनले २४ वर्षीय वीरगञ्ज घर भएका अनिकेतकुमार डंगोलसँग २०७९ भदौ ६ गते काठमाडौँ जिल्ल्ला अदालतबाट विवाह गरी त्यसैको आधारमा जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय पर्साबाट नेपाली अंगीकृत नागरिकता लिएको र त्यसपछि सम्बन्धविच्छेद गरेको अनुसन्धानमा देखिएको छ ।

अनुसन्धान अनुसार दुवैबीच खासै चिनजान थिएन र विवाहपछि पनि श्रीमान श्रीमतीको रूपमा बसेको पनि देखिएन । आर्थिक प्रलोभनमा कागजी विवाह भएको आशंका गरिएको छ ।

एलिनले पछि अर्का विदेशी नागरिकसँग विवाह गरिन् र उनलाई समेत नेपाल ल्याएको अनुसन्धानमा भेटिएको छ । उनले स्वीडेनी नागरिकता त्यागेको दाबी गरेपनि त्यसको प्रमाण पेस नगरेको बताइन्छ । नेपाली राहदानी प्रयोग गरेर भारत १६ पटक गएको र त्यहाँबाट स्वीडिस राहदानीमार्फत तेस्रो मुलुक गएको विवरणसमेत अनुसन्धानमा आएको छ ।

एलिनका विदेशी श्रीमानले गोफिका इन्टरनेसनल कार्गो प्रालि नामको कम्पनी २०८० जेठ १४ गते उद्योग विभागमा दर्ता कम्पनी खोलेर बिजनेस भिसा लिएको तर कारोबार नगरी कम्पनी बन्द गरेको विवरण पनि अनुसन्धानमा छ । नेपाली नागरिकता लिएकी एलिनले नेपाली युवासँग सम्बन्ध बिच्छेद गरी पुन आफ्नै श्रीमानसँग विवाह गरेको पाइएको छ । यसै विवाहको आधारमा उनले श्रीमान कार्ललाई समेत नेपाली अंगिकृत नागरिकता समेत दिलाउन सफल भएको पाइन्छ । एलिनसँग नेपालमा विहे गर्नु अघि कार्ल ११ पटक पर्यटक र ५ पटक व्यवसायिक भिसामा नेपाल आइसकेका थिए ।

एलिनका श्रीमानले नेपाली अंगीकृत नागरिकता लिँदासम्मको सबै विवरणहरू शंकास्पद रहेको देखिन्छ । यसबारे राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागले अनुसन्धान गरेर रिपोर्ट पनि दिएको छ । तर कानुनी रूपमा उनीहरूले सबै प्रक्रिया पूरा गरेर नेपाली नागरिकता समेत लिएकाले कारबाही प्रक्रिया भने अघि बढाउन सकेको छैनन ।

अर्को उदाहरण अमेरिकी नागरिक अमान्ड मैडा समर्स हुन् । उनले ९२ वर्षीय हर्कबहादुर घर्तीसँग विवाह गरेर वैवाहिक भिसामा नेपाल बसेकी थिइन् । उनी १५ वर्षजति नेपालमा बसेकी थिइन् ।

विवाहपछि अमान्ड ललितपुर महानगरपालिका–२५, सैंबुमा बसिन् र सन्ध्या कर्णको नाममा दर्ता भएको स्वालम्बन नामक एनजीओमा आबद्ध भइन् । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा उनले पाकिस्तानी नागरिक लर्ड किङ भिन्सेन्टलाई नेपालमा सेल्टर दिएको खुलेको बताइएको छ । भिन्सेन्ट २०२५ जनवरी २८ मा नेपाल आएका थिए र उनको पर्यटक भिसा मे १२ सम्म मात्रै थियो । तर भिसा सकिएको करिब एक महिनासम्म अमान्डले उनलाई आश्रय दिएको अनुसन्धानमा भेटियो ।

गुप्तचर सूचनाका आधारमा २०८३ जेठ २९ गते सैंबुबाट उनीहरू पक्राउ परे र पछि डिपोर्ट गरिए । अध्यागमन विभागका अनुसार सन् २०२५ मा मात्रै ५२३ विदेशी नागरिक डिपोर्ट भएका छन् ।

तीमध्ये चीनका १२०, बंगलादेशका ७५, अमेरिकाका ३५, बेलायतका २२, पाकिस्तानका १८ र अन्य देशका २५३ नागरिक छन् । ४५९ जना ओभरस्टे र ६४ जना शंकास्पद गतिविधिका कारण डिपोर्ट गरिएको विभागको तथ्यांक छ ।

यसरी डिपोर्ट गरिएकाहरु मध्यै धेरैले पहिला अध्ययन भिसा, व्यवसायिक भिसाको बहानामा लामो समय नेपालमा बसेर मिसनरीको रूपमा काम गर्ने प्रवृत्ति देखिएको छ । काठमाडौंलाई नेस्ट अफ स्पाई भनिन्छ । विभिन्न देशका गुप्तचर एजेन्सीहरूको ट्रान्जिट र सूचना संकलन केन्द्रका रूपमा समेत काठमाडौंलाई प्रयोग गर्ने गरिएको सुरक्षा विश्लेषण छ ।

नेपालमा हुने गतिविधिमा चिनियाँ चासो वा अमेरिकी रणनीतिक उद्देश्यका लागि सूचना संकलनका काम गरेको हुनसक्ने सुरक्षा संयन्त्रको विश्लेषण छ । त्यसैले पर्यटन, व्यवसाय, भाषा केन्द्र, एनजीओ वा विवाहको आवरणमा लामो समय बस्ने र त्यस क्रममा धार्मिक प्रचार, शंकास्पद गतिविधि वा राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामा असर पार्ने काम हुन सक्ने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: ‘गोदावरी महिला उद्यम विकास प्रतिष्ठान’को उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गोदावरी नगरपालिकामा नवनिर्मित ‘गोदावरी महिला उद्यम विकास प्रतिष्ठान’को आइतबार एक विशेष समारोहबीच उद्घाटन गरिएको छ ।

महिलाहरूलाई सीप विकास, उद्यमशीलता र आयआर्जनका अवसरहरूसँग जोड्दै आर्थिक रूपमा आत्मनिर्भर बनाउने उद्देश्यले प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना गरिएको हो । गोदावरी नगरपालिकाका उपप्रमुख मुना अधिकारीको अध्यक्षतामा सम्पन्न उक्त कार्यक्रममा नगर प्रमुख गजेन्द्र महर्जन प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी थिए ।

कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वडाका वडाध्यक्ष, जनप्रतिनिधि, महिला उद्यमी, सरोकारवाला संघ–संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि तथा स्थानीयको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो । समारोहमा स्थानीय महिला उद्यमीहरूले उत्पादन गरेका विभिन्न सामग्रीको प्रदर्शनीसमेत गरिएको थियो ।

नवनिर्मित प्रतिष्ठानलाई महिला उद्यमीहरूका लागि तालिम, उत्पादन, प्रदर्शनी तथा बजारीकरणको एकीकृत केन्द्रका रूपमा विकास गर्ने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

गोदावरी नगरपालिकाले महिलाहरूलाई शिक्षा, सीप र उद्यमशीलतामार्फत आत्मनिर्भर बनाउन अनौपचारिक शिक्षा कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन कार्यविधि २०८१ समेत जारी गरी अभियान सञ्चालन गरिरहेको छ । हालसम्म ४७ जना महिलाले प्लस टु उत्तीर्ण गरिसकेका छन् भने ११ जना स्नातक तहमा अध्ययनरत छन् ।

यस्तै, १४० भन्दा बढी महिला तह १ र २ मा अध्ययन गरिरहेका छन् । शिक्षाका साथै महिलाहरूलाई आयआर्जनमा जोड्न नगरपालिकाले ढाका बुनाई, साबुन तथा सरसफाइ सामग्री निर्माण, सिलाइ–कटाइ, हस्तकला, अचार, टपरी र स्यानिटरी प्याड उत्पादनजस्ता विभिन्न सीपमूलक तालिमहरू सञ्चालन गर्दै आएको छ ।

महिलाहरूलाई केवल तालिममा मात्र सीमित नराखी शिक्षित, सीपयुक्त, स्वरोजगार र पूर्ण रूपमा आत्मनिर्भर बनाउनु यस अभियानको लक्ष्य रहेको छ ।

articles.title: दोलखामा दिनभर धार्मिक परिक्रमा, रातभर लाखे नाच !
articles.summary:
दोलखा । प्राचीन तथा ऐतिहासिक नगरी दोलखामा धार्मिक सहिष्णुता र सांस्कृतिक सद्भावको प्रतीक मानिने परम्परागत हिले जात्रा अर्थात् गुउँला पर्व हर्षोल्लासका साथ मनाइँदैछ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदा अर्थात् घण्टाकर्ण (गाठामा) को तेस्रो दिनदेखि सुरु भएको यो ऐतिहासिक पर्वका कारण यतिबेला दोलखा बजार २४ सै घण्टा सांस्कृतिक रौनकमा झुमिरहेको छ ।

बिहानैदेखि गुञ्जने परम्परागत बाजा, धार्मिक परिक्रमा र दिउँसोदेखि रातिसम्म देखाइने फरक स्वरूपका लाखे नाचले प्राचीन नगरी दोलखा यतिबेला गुञ्जायमान बनेको छ । घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् स्थानीय भाषामा ‘गाठामा’को तेस्रो दिन, श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि दोलखामा गुउँला जात्राको औपचारिक सुरुवात हुन्छ ।

माथिल्लो र तल्लो टोलका बेग्लाबेग्लै डापा खलक परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित बिहानै सांस्कृतिक परिक्रमामा निस्कन्छन् । स्थानीय भाषामा देउ उय भनिने यो परिक्रमा कागे अष्टमीका दिन समापन हुन्छ ।

पूजा सामग्री बोकेका ज्येष्ठ नागरिकसहितको टोली स्वयंभू चैत्य र कोर्छे टोलबाट सुरु भई भीमेश्वर, कालीमन्दिर, त्रिपुरा सुन्दरी, राजकुलेश्वर तलेजु, नक्छे चैत्य, गणेश मन्दिर र मच्चिछन्द्रनाथ मन्दिर हुँदै पुनः स्वयंभू चैत्य पुगेर टुंगिन्छ । जात्रा मनाउँदा हिन्दू र बौद्ध दुवै धार्मिकस्थलको समान रूपमा परिक्रमा गरिन्छ ।

दिउँसोदेखि दोलखा बजारमा लाखे नाचको रौनक सुरु हुन्छ । एउटै जात्रामा चार फरक स्वरूपका लाखे प्रदर्शन हुने भएकाले दोलखाको लाखे देशभरमै विशेष मानिन्छ ।

दिउँसो ३ देखि ५ बजेसम्म ‘जोङ डाकस’ निकालिन्छ । यसमा हात दुई जना दाउरेले समातेर दर्शकलाई लखेट्दै मनोरञ्जन गराउँछन् । आसुरी शक्तिमाथि विजयको कथा भन्ने नेपाल डाकस भने राति मात्र नाचिन्छ । वर्षमा एक दिन रक्षाबन्धनका दिन निकालिने ‘ड्वाकु डाकस’ ठूलो लाखे हो । फरक मुखुण्डो लगाइने यसलाई महाकालीका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ ।

गाईजात्रादेखि पञ्चमीसम्म ‘माझीपा डाकस’ पनि प्रदर्शन गरिन्छ । डोरीले बाँधेर लाखेलाई नचाउने र माझीहरूले नियन्त्रण गर्न खोजेको लोककथाको अभिनय यसमा देखाइन्छ । पुस्तौँदेखि चल्दै आएको यस अमूर्त कला र संस्कृति संरक्षणमा स्थानीय युवाको सक्रियता उदाहरणीय छ ।

articles.title: माननीयको अभिब्यक्तिले सुरक्षा संगठनको बदनाम
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । मुलुकको शान्ति, सुरक्षा र कानुन कार्यान्वयनको मुख्य जिम्मेवारी बोकेको नेपाल प्रहरी अहिले दोहोरो दबाबमा परेको छ । एकातिर गत बर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गतेको आन्दोलनका क्रममा संगठनले भोगेको भौतिक तथा मनोवैज्ञानिक क्षतिको असर अझै पूर्णरूपमा मेटिन सकेको छैन भने, अर्कोतिर राजनीतिक वृत्तबाटै संगठनको नेतृत्व र कार्यशैलीमाथि प्रश्न उठाउने क्रम तीव्र बनेको छ ।

राज्यकै प्रमुख निकायहरु कार्यपालिका र ब्यवस्थापिकाबाटै प्रहरी संगठनको बदनाम गर्ने कार्यले संगठनको मनोबल झनै गिराएको छ । सार्वजनिक पदमा बसेका व्यक्तिले उठाउने प्रश्नले सधैं सार्वजनिक चासो निम्त्याउँछ, विशेषगरी त्यो प्रश्न राज्यको कुनै संवेदनशील निकायविरुद्ध उठाइएको हुँदा गत बुधबार सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको बैठकमा रास्वपाका सांसद खगेन्द्र सुनारले नेपाल प्रहरीको सामग्री खरिद प्रक्रियामा प्रश्न उठाउँदै प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई नै कठघरामा उभ्याए ।

जुत्ता, मोजा, पोशाकदेखि लाठी खरिदसम्ममा आर्थिक अनियमितता भएको आशय दिँदै उनले तत्काल निष्पक्ष छानबिनको माग गरे । आइजीपी कार्कीले तत्काल प्रतिवाद गरे । खरिद प्रक्रियामा कुनै अनियमितता नभएको दाबी गर्दै तथ्यहीन आरोप लगाएर कर्मचारीको मनोबल कमजोर नबनाउन आग्रह गरे ।

त्यसपछि सांसद सुनारकै आफ्नै कानुनी पृष्ठभूमिबारे सार्वजनिक बहस सुरु भयो — प्रश्न उठाउने व्यक्ति स्वयं कति चोखो छ ? आईजीपी कार्कीले सांसद सुनारविरुद्ध नै आएका उजुरीहरूको चाङ औंल्याए । सुनारविरुद्ध माननीयदेखि दयनीयसम्मका व्यक्तिहरूले विभिन्न प्रकृतिका उजुरी दिएको र, आरोपको पोको खोलिदिन सक्ने चेतावनी दिए ।

सर्वत्र आलोचित खगेन्द्र अझै ‘अराजक’

लेखा समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीमाथि खगेन्द्र सुनारले उठाएको प्रश्नले मात्रै खगेन्द्र चर्चा र विवादमा आएका होइनन् । प्रहरी संगठन विरुद्ध पटक पटक सार्वजनिक उनको अभिब्यक्तिले सांसद सुनार आलोचित छन् ।

२०८३ वैशाख ७ गते सिन्धुली सुनकोशी गाउँपालिका–३ जुम्लीडाँडा निवासी २३ वर्षीय श्रीकृष्ण विक खुर्कोटस्थित प्रहरीको हिरासतमै मृत्यु भएको घटनामा जनप्रतिनिधिको हैसियतमा सिन्धुली पुगेका सुनाले एकतर्फी आरोप लगाउँदै सिन्धुलीका एसपीको कठालो नै समातेर घिसार्नुपर्ने अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए ।

सांसद हुनुपूर्व सुनारले एक वर्षअघि माइतीघरबाट समेत जिल्ला प्रहरी परिसर काठमाडौंका एकजना डीएसपी विरुद्ध अर्मयादित अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए । त्यो बेला जहाँ पनि उनी हातमा नेल र निधारमा नवसेना लेखिएको फेटा बाँधेर सांकेतिक विरोधमा देखिन्थे । यो पटक संसदीय समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीविरुद्ध पनि उही शैलीमा आक्रोश पोखेका थिए ।

सुनारविरुद्ध तीन मुद्दा अदालतमा विचाराधिन

सांसद खगेन्द्र माथि अहिले पनि तीनवटा मुद्दा अदालतमै विचाराधीन छ । दैलेखको नारायण नगरपालिका–२ भैसेखोरका खगेन्द्र प्रतिनिधि सभाको चुनावमा भने बाँके क्षेत्र नम्बर ३ बाट निर्वाचित भएका हुन् । उनीमाथि सुर्खेत प्रहरीले २०८० को असारमा पक्राउ गरेर सार्वजनिक शान्तिविरुद्धको कसुरमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

त्यो बेला जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय सुर्खेतले २० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी लिएर छाडेको थियो । त्यसको एक वर्षपछि पुनः २०८१ असारमै सुर्खेतकै अस्पतालका डाक्टरहरुमाथि अभद्र व्यवहार तथा तोडफोडको मुद्दा हाल सुर्खेत जिल्ला अदालतमा विचाराधीन अवस्थामा छ । २०८२ साउनमा काभ्रेकी एक महिलामाथि सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत चरित्र हत्या गर्ने खालको पोष्ट गरेको आरोपमा उनीमाथि काभ्रे प्रहरीले साइबर अपराधमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

साउन ५ गते पक्राउ पुर्जी लिए पनि उनी पक्राउ भने परेनन् । पछि मुद्दा अदालत दर्ता भएपछि उनी काभ्रे जिल्ला अदालतमा हाजिर भएका थिए । काभ्रे अदालतले समेत सुनारलाई ५० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी बुझाएर मात्रै छाड्ने आदेश गरेका थिए । हालसम्म पनि मुद्दा टुंगो लागेको छैन ।

सुनारको प्रहरी नेतृत्वमाथि भएको व्यक्तिगत आक्षेप र अमर्यादित व्यवहार विवाद गृहमन्त्री हुँदै सभामुखसम्म पुगेको छ । आइजिपीसहित आठ एआइजी र एक डिआइजीले प्रहरी संगठनकै मनोबल खस्किएको भन्दै संसदीय छानबिनमा विधि र मर्यादा पालना गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन् ।

बेनामे उजुरीको भरमा संसदीय समितिमा बोलाएर संगठनकै मानमर्दन हुने गरी हुर्मत लिएको गुनासो समेत गरेका छन् । प्रहरी अधिकारी मात्र होइन, गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङसमेत सुनारको ब्यवहारले रुष्ट छन् ।

प्रहरी संगठनबाटै ‘माननीय’विरुद्ध खेद ब्यक्त

प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्य सुनारको अराजक अभिब्यक्तिको सिंगो प्रहरी संगठनले नै खेद प्रकट गरेको छ । नेपाल प्रहरी पूर्वप्रहरी संगठन प्रमुख मञ्चले विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर सुरक्षा निकाय र यसको नेतृत्वमाथि भएका व्यक्तिलक्षित टीकाटिप्पणीप्रति खेद प्रकट गरेको छ ।

भने पूर्वप्रहरी कर्मचारी परिषद्, पूर्वसशस्त्र प्रहरी संघ र सुरक्षा तथा न्याय अध्ययन केन्द्रले संयुक्त विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर यस्ता गतिविधिले सुरक्षाकर्मीको मनोबल खस्कने र राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामै असर पर्ने स्पष्ट गरेका छन् । साथै ती संस्थाहरूले संसदीय समितिमा बोलाउँदा पदीय गरिमा, सम्मान र व्यावसायिक मर्यादा कायम राख्न सुझाएका छन् ।

अझै पुरिएको छैन भदौ २४ को घाउ

नेपाल प्रहरीका लागि २०८२ भदौ २३ र २४ गते घटनाको घाउ अझै पुरिएको छैन । त्यो घटनाले संगठनको भौतिक संरचना, हतियार, कार्यालय र प्रहरी कर्मचारीको सुरक्षामाथि नै ठूलो चुनौती खडा गरेको छ ।

उक्त आन्दोलनका क्रममा काठमाडौँ उपत्यकाका मात्र १ सय ५३ प्रहरी कार्यालयमा आगजनी, १७ वटा प्रहरी वृत्त क्षतिग्रस्त,१ हजार १ सय हतियार लुटिपाट,३ जना प्रहरीको मृत्यु र प्रहरी कर्मचारीले ज्यान जोगाउन बर्दी फुकालेर भाग्नुपर्ने अवस्था आएको थियो ।

सुरक्षा संगठन र कर्मचारीको मनोबल बढाउनुपर्नेमा सत्तारुढ दलबाट नै यस्ता खाले अभिव्यक्तिले संगठनको मनोबल गिर्दो अवस्थामा पुगेको पूर्व प्रहरी अधिकारीको भनाई छ ।

सांसदको काम प्रश्न उठाउनु नै हो, तर प्रश्न उठाउने नाममा प्रमाणविनाका आरोप लगाउनु र आरोप प्रमाणित नहुँदै त्यसलाई सत्यका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्नु जिम्मेवार राजनीतिक अभ्यास होइन । खगेन्द्र सुनार हिजो आन्दोलनकारी भए पनि आज जनताका प्रतिनिधि हुन् ।

त्यसैले विना आधार राज्यको जिम्मावार निकायहरुको बदनाम गर्दा सुरक्षा संगठनको मात्र होइन, स्वयम् माननीयको ओज घटाउँछ । प्रहरीलाई प्रश्न गरौँ, तर प्रमाणसहित ।

प्रहरीलाई जवाफदेही बनाऔँ, तर संस्थागत रूपमा । प्रहरी कमजोर हुँदा कमजोर हुने प्रहरी प्रमुख मात्र होइन, सिंगो राज्य हो । प्रहरी संगठनका भित्रका कमजोरीहरु सुधार हुनु पर्छ नै, सांसद सुनारको आफू पनि सुध्रिन जरुरी छ ।

articles.title: पूर्वी नाकाबाट विदेशी पर्यटक बढे, सबैभन्दा धेरै भुटानी
articles.summary:
झापा । पूर्वी नेपालको प्रमुख स्थलमार्ग काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा ८६ देशका ९ हजार ४४७ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल भित्रिएका छन्। अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाको तथ्याङ्कअनुसार यो संख्या दैनिक औसत करिब २६ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेको हो ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा काँकरभिट्टा नाकाबाट नेपाल प्रवेश गर्ने विदेशी पर्यटकमा भुटान, अमेरिका, थाइल्याण्ड, अष्ट्रेलिया, बेलायत, क्यानडा, जर्मनी, फ्रान्स, जापान र रुसलगायत देशका नागरिक छन् । कुल आगन्तुकमध्ये भुटानी नागरिकको हिस्सा सबैभन्दा ठूलो छ । ४ हजार ९९४ जना भुटानी नागरिक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् ।

जुन कुल पर्यटक संख्याको करिब ५३ प्रतिशत हो । त्यस्तै २ हजार १५२ जना अमेरिकी नागरिकले काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । यो कुल आगन्तुकको करिब २३ प्रतिशत हो । भारतका नागरिकलाई नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न भिसा आवश्यक नपर्ने भएकाले उनीहरूलाई तेस्रो मुलुकका पर्यटकसम्बन्धी तथ्याङ्कमा समावेश गरिएको छैन ।

महिनागत तथ्याङ्कअनुसार सबैभन्दा बढी विदेशी पर्यटक पुसमा १ हजार ८५० जना र सबैभन्दा कम भदौमा २१६ जना नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । अध्यागमन कार्यालयले पुस र माघलाई प्रमुख पर्यटकीय याम मानेको छ ।

पर्यटकको आगमन उत्साहजनक भएपनि बसाइ छोटो हुने गरेको होटल व्यवसायी बताउँछन। पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यमा पर्यटकलाई केही दिन रोक्न सके झापा, इलाम, ताप्लेजुङलगायत जिल्लाको पर्यटन तथा होटल व्यवसायमा उल्लेख्य योगदान पुग्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ छ ।

पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यको अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार र सीमा नाकामै यातायात, होटल तथा भ्रमणसम्बन्धी सूचना उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने पर्यटन व्यवसायी कुन्दन निरौला बताउँछन् ।

अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाले सन् २०२४ अगस्टदेखि पूर्ण रूपमा अध्यागमन सेवा सञ्चालन गरेको थियो । सेवा प्रभावकारी भएपछि विदेशी पर्यटकको आगमन क्रमशः बढेको सूचना अधिकारी इन्द्रकुमार राजवंशी बताउँछन् ।

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार, पर्यटन सूचना केन्द्र र आकर्षक प्याकेज निर्माणसँगै संघ, प्रदेश र स्थानीय तहबीच समन्वय गर्न सके विदेशी पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउन सकिने देखिन्छ । यसबाट होटल, यातायात, ट्राभल्स, हस्तकला तथा स्थानीय उत्पादनको बजारसमेत लाभान्वित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: राँगाको सिङबाट बन्ने गुँला पर्वको मुख्य बाजा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेवार समुदायका विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीको प्रमुख सांस्कृतिक पर्व गुँला बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । एक महिनासम्म मनाइने पर्वमा भक्तजनले परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित चैत्य, विहार र मन्दिरको परिक्रमा गर्दै बुद्धको पूजा–आराधना गर्ने गर्दछन् ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका परम्परागत नेवार वस्ती र टोलहरुमा अब एक महिनासम्म सडक वा गल्लीहरुमा विहान मानिसहरुको चहलपहल शुरु नहुँदै सुनिने छ, धिमे, भुस्या, बाँसुरी र न्याकुँको सुमधुर आवाज । अनि बाजाको यही धुन पछ्याउँदै मानिसहरू चैत्यतर्फ अघि बढिरहेका हुने छन् । यो गुँला पर्वको अवसरमा देखिने दृश्य हो ।

नेवार समुदायमा पनि विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीले मनाउने गुँला पर्व बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि भाद्र शुक्ल प्रतिपदासम्म चल्ने यो पर्व करिब एक महिनासम्म धार्मिक र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकालाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ ।

गुँला शब्दको अर्थ आफैमा रोचक पनि छ । नेपाल भाषामा ‘गुँ’ को अर्थ नौ र ‘ला’ को अर्थ महिना भन्ने गरिन्छ । नेपाल संवतको नवौँ महिनामा मनाइने भएकाले यसको नाम गुँला रहन गएको मानिन्छ । गुँलाको वास्तविक आकर्षण बिहानै सुरु हुने यात्रामा देखिन्छ । भक्तजनहरू परम्परागत बाजा बजाउँदै विभिन्न चैत्य, विहार, बहाः र बहीको परिक्रमा गर्छन् ।

काठमाडौंको स्वयम्भू, बौद्ध, पाटनलगायतका धार्मिक तथा ऐतिहासिक स्थलमा गुँला पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखिन्छ । एउटा समूह धिमे बजाउँदै अघि बढिरहेको हुन्छ । यसमा कसैले भुस्या बजाइरहेको हुन्छ भने कसैले न्याकुँको गहिरो आवाज निकालिरहेको हुन्छ । यही दृश्यले गुँलालाई काठमाडौँका अन्य धेरै जात्रा र पर्वहरुभन्दा फरक बनाएको छ ।

गुँला पूजा र परिक्रमा गर्ने पर्व मात्रै होइन । संगीत जोडिएको उपत्यकाको जीवित संस्कृति पनि हो । विशेषगरी न्याकुँ बाजा गुँलाको पहिचानसँग जोडिएको छ । राँगाको सिङबाट बनाइने यो बाजा हेर्दा साधारण देखिए पनि यसको ध्वनि निकै विशिष्ट हुन्छ ।

परम्परागत रूपमा धार्मिक यात्राहरुमा यसको प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ । त्यसैगरी धिमे, बाँसुरी, भुस्या र धाः लगायतका बाजासँगै बज्दा यी आवाजले पनि गुँला पर्वमा सांगीतिक समूहको स्वरूप लिन्छन् । पछिल्लो समय यस्ता जात्रा पर्वमा नयाँ पुस्ताको सहभागिता पनि बढिरहेको छ । नयाँ पूस्ताको सहभागितासँगै परम्परागत पर्व र संस्कृति पुस्तान्तरण पनि हुँदैछन् ।

गुँला धार्मिक पर्व मात्रैमा सीमित छैन । सामाजिकरुपमा खेतीपातीको मुख्य काम सकिएको समयसँग पनि यो पर्व जोडिएको छ । मानिसहरू केही फुर्सदिला हुने यही समयमा समुदाय भेला हुने, भेटघाट गर्ने र सामूहिक रूपमा धार्मिक गतिविधिमा सहभागी हुने अवसर पनि गुँलाले जुटाइ दिएको छ ।

बौद्ध परम्परामा वर्षायामको साधना र धार्मिक अभ्याससँग पनि गुँला समयको सम्बन्ध जोडिन्छ । त्यसैले यो अवधि पूजा, ध्यान, पाठ, दान र पुण्यकर्मका लागि विशेष मानिन्छ । यसको अर्को पक्ष के भने गुँला पर्वमा हुने चैत्य परिक्रमा एउटा यात्रा मात्रै होइन ।

उपत्यकाका विभिन्न स्थानीय धार्मिक स्थललाई जोड्ने सांस्कृतिक नेटवर्क जस्तो पनि हो । एउटा टोलबाट अर्को टोल, एउटा बहाःबाट अर्को चैत्यसम्म बाजाको धुनले यी ठाउँहरूलाई जोडिरहेको हुन्छ । काठमाडौंलाई मन्दिरै–मन्दिरको सहर भनिन्छ । तर गुँला पर्वले कामठाडौँ बाजा, बहाः, बही र चैत्यहरूको पनि सहर हो भन्ने प्रमाण पनि दिन्छ । एक महिनासम्म बज्ने यी बाजाहरु पुर्खाको स्मृति हुन्, धार्मिक आस्था हुन् र पहिचानको आवाज हुन् ।

articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: RSP chair Lamichhane tells CIAA to act if government officials obstruct its work
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah and his secretariat have come under parliamentary scrutiny over allegations that officials of the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority were held at the Prime Minister’s Office for seven hours and pressured to prosecute officials in a passport procurement case.

Rabi Lamichhane, chair of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party, said on Thursday that obstructing the CIAA’s work was an offence. He urged the constitutional commission to act if the government had interfered with its investigation.

Speaking at a meeting of the State Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Lamichhane said that, as the leader of the party running the government, he would not object if the CIAA took action against anyone found to have obstructed its work.

“I want to tell the entire CIAA team that if there has been any weakness on the part of our government and if that has created any obstruction to your work, creating obstacles to investigation and prosecution is itself a form of crime,” Lamichhane said. “If you have clear grounds, reasons and evidence of such a problem, you can proceed with the necessary action.”

Lamichhane said the ruling party would not exert pressure on the commission if anyone was found to have interfered with its work.

“If there are people involved in such activities and you have the grounds and reasons, you will face no pressure or influence of any kind from us,” the RSP chief said.

He also said the government had a responsibility to ensure that constitutional bodies such as the CIAA could work independently and without interference.

Shah and his secretariat have been accused of summoning CIAA officials, including Chief Commissioner Prem Kumar Rai, to the Prime Minister’s Office on June 15 and keeping them there for around seven hours while pressuring the commission to prosecute officials in connection with a passport procurement contract.

Shah took up the issue at the RSP general convention in Chitwan on June 21, saying that the CIAA could be questioned for five hours and, if necessary, for five years.

“If the CIAA [leadership] needs to be held for five hours to answer questions and give advice, then we can keep it for not just five hours, but five years, if necessary,” Shah said. “We will not do anything against the rules.”

The CIAA had not publicly commented on the alleged incident until Thursday.

Chief Commissioner Rai said the CIAA had been invited to the Prime Minister’s Office for discussions on the passport issue.

“The prime minister may have invited the concerned parties for discussions and suggestions on the passport issue. We also participated in the discussion,” Rai said. “Some areas requiring improvement were identified, and some improvements were subsequently made.”

Rai said the case had already been registered and prosecuted.

“As the case has already been registered and prosecution taken place, the legal aspects are now for the relevant authorities to deal with,” Rai said, elaborating on the legality of the PMO meeting. “The prosecution document itself clearly states the grounds on which the case was pursued. Therefore, I do not want to go into the matter unnecessarily.”

Responding to allegations that the prosecution had been initiated under pressure from the Prime Minister’s Office, Rai said the case had not been pursued without legal grounds.

“Looking at the relevant documents, it is clear that the prosecution was not initiated without grounds or without shortcomings being identified,” he said.

The prime minister’s secretariat has also been accused of pressuring the CIAA to file a case against officials deemed responsible for irregularities in the passport procurement process and to seek arrest warrants against them.

Officials at the commission were reportedly pressured into arresting Tirtha Raj Aryal, director general of the Department of Passports, and Sunil Kumar KC, a director at the department.

Lamichhane’s comments come against that backdrop. He said the CIAA should act if it believed the government or people associated with it had obstructed the commission’s work.

Rai attended the committee meeting along with commissioners Jaya Bahadur Chand, Hari Paudel and Sumitra Shrestha Amatya and senior CIAA officials.

Opposition lawmakers asked the anti-graft officials to explain what had happened at the Prime Minister’s Office and whether the commission had been subjected to pressure. Some lawmakers stressed that the CIAA should be allowed to work independently.

Harka Raj Rai, chair of the Shram Sanskriti Party and a committee member, said concerns over the alleged pressure on the CIAA had been raised both in Parliament and in the committee.

He questioned who would hold the prime minister accountable if the head of the executive himself abused his authority.

“If the prime minister keeps you confined for seven hours, that is an abuse of authority. Who will take action against the prime minister for abusing that authority? He is the head of the executive himself,” lawmaker Rai said.

He said the episode had raised questions about whether the CIAA could operate independently and without fear.

Opposition lawmakers questioned the independence of the commission saying that it appeared to be under political pressure. They demanded an explanation of its dealings with the Prime Minister’s Office.

CPN-UML lawmaker Padma Aryal said the commission may be working under pressure.

“It appears that the CIAA is under pressure and influence, with attempts being made to use it for political purposes,” Aryal said.

She said constitutional bodies must be allowed to work independently if the government is to deliver on its promises of good governance.

Nepali Congress lawmaker Arjun Narsingh KC said efforts were being made to weaken the CIAA.

RSP lawmaker Amaresh Kumar Singh said the CIAA had the authority to investigate the prime minister and ministers and that it should not be answerable to the executive.

Singh also urged CIAA officials to assert the commission’s constitutional autonomy when summoned by the prime minister or ministers.

“Do not go if they summon you. The CIAA does not fall under the Prime Minister’s Office. Even if you receive a letter, tell them that you are an independent constitutional body,” Singh said.

articles.title: Only 53 percent of UML workers renew party membership
articles.summary:
The number of CPN-UML members has fallen sharply, with only about 53 percent of committed workers renewing their membership, as the party struggles to rebuild its organisation shaken after last year's Gen Z movement.

According to figures provided by provincial committees, 359,000 members renewed their membership by the mid-August deadline. The figures are still being updated, party officials said.

The party had 686,700 members on its rolls, meaning that around 327,000 have not renewed their membership.

UML leaders attribute the low renewal rate to growing dissatisfaction among some cadres, a lack of opportunities for those who have not benefited from the party’s organisational structure, and limited space for younger members.

The party led by KP Sharma Oli was in power in a coalition government with the Nepali Congress. The September revolt ousted Oli as prime minister last year.

In the general convention held in December last year, Oli was reelected the party chair, despite the message of the movement that a younger generation should lead Nepal’s traditional political parties.

The March elections held earlier this year left the party a distant third force, as an overwhelming majority went in favour of the Rastriya Swatantra Party. The Nepali Congress also shrank to a much smaller size, even as it holds the second place in the federal parliament.

The spectacular fall in popular vote—to 1.45 million from 2.84 million in the 2022 election—led the UML to reexamine its organisational base. Leaders call the renewal process a test of the listed members’ commitment to the party, especially following its loss of support base as seen in the March elections.

UML General Secretary Shankar Pokharel says the party needs policies that give both older and younger members a sense of future within the organisation.

“We need to create conditions in which young people see their future in the party,” Pokharel told Kantipur last week. “That is possible only through restructuring the party.”

Pokharel, who is also the secretary of a panel led by vice-chair Ram Bahadur Thapa for party restructuring, has proposed a system that brings three generations together and creates a swift mechanism for leadership development and transfer.

A breakdown of the membership renewal figures shows a uniform pattern of update.

The Sudurpaschim Province has recorded the lowest renewal rate. Of 63,110 members, only about 17,000 sought renewal. Provincial secretary Ran Bahadur Chand said the tally could rise to around 21,000 after paper renewals are entered into the system.

In Koshi Province, 62,000 of 114,766 members went for renewal, putting the rate at about 54 percent. Madhesh recorded 60,000 renewals from a membership size of 156,195. Provincial secretary Manoj Paudel said the rate could cross 60 percent.

Paudel said the lower figures point to a tighter verification process. In the past, he said, a single person could renew membership for hundreds of people, whereas members are now required to renew in person.

Bagmati recorded about 66,000 renewals from 114,566 members. In Gandaki, 30,500 of the 56,052 members had renewed their status, although provincial leaders expect the figure to approach 60 percent after further updates.

Lumbini reported about 42,000 renewals from 80,579 members, a rate of 52.12 percent. Karnali recorded about 28,000 renewals among 48,538 members, or 57.69 percent.

In Kathmandu Valley, the capital committee covering Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur reported 23,500 renewals from 39,159 members, or about 60 percent. The party’s liaison department, which represents members from outside districts living in Kathmandu, reported more than 8,000 renewals from 13,783 members.

UML Secretary and Organisation Department chief Bhanu Bhakta Dhakal described the renewal drive as encouraging but said the final nationwide figure was still being compiled.

“The membership renewal has been encouraging. Updated figures from the provinces have yet to come,” Dhakal said.

He said the party was also cleaning up its membership records, particularly in Madhesh, where large numbers of people had previously been enrolled in bulk.

The latest figures are well below the numbers claimed by the UML in previous years. At its statute convention in Godawari, Lalitpur, in 2025, General Secretary Pokharel reported 662,961 members after renewal.

Before that convention, the UML had claimed more than 1.26 million members. After verification and updating, the figures fell to about 682,000, with 662,961 members recorded as having renewed ahead of the convention.

The latest figures suggest the party is experiencing a significant contraction in its active membership base. Krishna Pokharel, a professor of political science, said the party leadership’s policies and working style shape the mindset of ordinary members. He said UML chair Oli had failed to inspire cadres, both in and out of government.

“Cadres assess their future by looking at the leadership. If they believe the leadership can take the party forward, they remain engaged,” he said. Repeated failures also eroded the leadership’s appeal among voters and cadres.

Pokharel said honest members had become disillusioned after seeing opportunistic leaders benefit from party positions while their expectations went unmet. “Some cadres may have left after seeing little prospect of the UML returning to power,” he added.

articles.title: Registrar vacancies delay budget approvals at major universities
articles.summary:
Major universities in the country have entered the new fiscal year without approved budgets as the government is yet to appoint registrars, leaving institutions dependent on acting officials and restricted interim spending arrangements.

Tribhuvan University, Purbanchal University, Pokhara University, Mid-Western University, Sudurpashchim University, Agriculture and Forestry University and Nepal Sanskrit University are among those with vacant registrar posts. Lumbini Buddhist University and Nepal Open University face wider leadership gaps.

The vacancies followed the government’s May 2 decision to remove senior university officials through an ordinance, in an attempt to replace politically appointed officials and introduce competitive selection. Acting officials were later tasked with keeping institutions functioning.

At Tribhuvan University, the country’s largest, the consequences are particularly serious. Its budget for the fiscal year 2026-27 was due to be approved by the first week of August, but the Senate has yet to meet.

“Anarchy looms because the government has shown no interest in appointing the rector and registrar,” said a TU professor. “The registrar prepares the budget and presents it to the Senate for approval. For now, the university is operating with an advance budget.”

The TU has a regular annual budget of around Rs26 billion. An advance budget can cover administrative expenses, but capital expenditure cannot proceed normally until an approval of the spending plan.

The delay is also affecting students. The Senate normally approves the graduation list along with the annual budget. About 95,000 students who have completed their studies under the TU are waiting to be enlisted for degree awards.

“Students can receive their original certificates only after the graduation list is approved,” the professor said. “Until that happens, certificates cannot be printed. The government has not paid attention to this, and the university is becoming disorganised.”

TU Examination Controller Laxman Paudel said the graduation list had already been prepared but remained pending because the Senate had not met. After approval, students apply to attend the graduation ceremony, allowing the university to print certificates and arrange gowns.

TU spokesperson Nabindra Bhandari said the university was preparing to call the Senate soon to approve the budget and graduation list.

TU Vice-chancellor Bhola Thapa recommended candidates for rector and registrar several weeks ago, according to university and education ministry officials. The names were sent to the Prime Minister’s Office, but appointments have not yet been made. Science and Technology Dean Shankar Khanal is acting rector, while Management Dean Mahananda Chalise has been assigned as acting registrar.

Under university law, the vice-chancellor recommends the rector and registrar and the prime minister, as chancellor, appoints them. The prolonged vacancies have left universities waiting for central decisions on posts essential to financial and administrative functioning.

Pokhara University is experiencing a similar problem. Vice-chancellor Devendra Adhikari said the university could not approve its new budget because the Senate could not be constituted without the registrar and other officials.

“The budget has to be approved by the Senate. The registrar and other members needed for the Senate are still awaiting appointment,” said Adhikari. “The law allows us to spend up to 33 percent of the previous year’s total budget and seek approval later. We are therefore carrying out administrative work under that provision.”

Adhikari said the name for registrar had been finalised but the ministry had not made the appointment.

Purbanchal University is also waiting for its registrar. Vice-chancellor Sujan Babu Marahatta said the recommendation had been made and the university would bring its budget as soon as the appointment was completed.

The education ministry says the process is moving ahead. Diwakar Bhujel, an undersecretary at Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel’s secretariat, said recommendations for registrars had been received from five universities.

“Names have been received for the appointment of registrars. We are studying them and the appointment process is under way,” said Bhujel. The ministry said the process is on to appoint registrars in Tribhuvan, Purbanchal, Pokhara, Mid-Western and Sudurpashchim universities.

Mid-Western University has avoided the immediate budget problem. Vice-chancellor Rajan Suwal said its budget had already been approved by acting officials, but other administrative work was being held up.

“The registrar and deans need to be appointed, but the work is stalled because the registrar has not been appointed from above,” said Suwal. “I do not know why the appointment has not happened.”

Sudurpashchim University Vice-chancellor Kisan Datta Bhatta said the university had sent a name for the registrar and expected an appointment soon. Its budget had already been approved by the previous acting officials, he said.

Agriculture and Forestry University has also approved its budget. Vice-chancellor Rishi Ram Kattel said no formal recommendation had yet been made for the registrar and Prof Subir Singh was continuing as acting registrar.

“The registrar appointment process has not been started and no recommendation has been made,” said Kattel. “The Senate met in June and approved the budget. There is no immediate plan to appoint a registrar; the university is functioning through the acting arrangement.”

Kathmandu University had likewise approved its 2026-27 budget in June when its Senate met for the graduation ceremony. Acting registrar Rajiv Shrestha said the budget was passed at that meeting. Prof Bibek Baral was appointed vice-chancellor in August, while Shrestha was retained as acting registrar until further arrangement.

The May ordinance removed senior officials from 16 universities and several health science academies. The government said it wanted to end political patronage, while academics criticised the move for increasing executive control over universities.

The government has since appointed vice-chancellors at several universities, including Tribhuvan, Purbanchal, Pokhara, Mid-Western, Sudurpashchim and Agriculture and Forestry. Registrar appointments lag.

At Lumbini Buddhist University, the government plans to restart the vice-chancellor selection process after receiving too few applications. At Nepal Open University, the process had stalled because the University Grants Commission chairperson’s post was vacant. The government has since appointed Prof Khadga KC there.

articles.title: Nepal’s journalism classrooms are emptying out
articles.summary:
The classrooms that once drew aspiring reporters from across Nepal are falling quiet. Fewer students are choosing journalism, a sign of growing troubles in the country’s media industry.

At Janapremi World School in Bhaktapur, journalism was once one of the college’s defining programmes. Since it began offering journalism at the plus-two level in 2009, students from 57 districts have studied there. At its peak, 76 students enrolled in a single batch.

Many alumni went on to work in mainstream media. But the programme has not admitted a new student for four years.

“We ran the programme even when there were only 19 students in the last batch,” said Nilesh Acharya, principal of Janapremi World School. “But as the student numbers kept falling, we had no option but to shut down the department.”

The college continues to attract a significant number of students to its science, management and law programmes at grades 11 and 12, he said.

The experience is not isolated. Data from the National Examination Board show that the number of schools offering journalism and mass communication at grades 11 and 12 fell from 209 in academic year 2022-23 to 105 in 2026-27. Student enrolment also dropped from 4,303 students to 1,303 over the same period.

The decline extends to university education. Tribhuvan University’s Office of the Controller of Examinations recorded 2,760 students enrolling in journalism and mass communication at bachelor’s level in 2020-21. By 2024-25, the figure had fallen to 1,132.

Enrolment followed the same downward path: 3,097 in 2021-22; 2,059 in 2022-23; 1,277 in 2023-24 and 1,132 in 2024-25.

In the academic year 2020-21, journalism and mass communication were taught at 74 campuses affiliated with Tribhuvan University across the country. The number fell to 61 in 2023-24 and declined further to just 57 by 2024-25.

Purbanchal University has seen a similar trend. Its journalism and mass communication enrolment fell from 122 students in 2021-22 to 74 in 2025-26.

At St Xavier’s College in Maitighar, journalism department head Chun Bahadur Gurung has seen the change in his own classroom. “We have taught as many as 34 students in a batch, but now the average is around 14 or 15,” he said.

Teachers and college administrators point to several reasons: shrinking number of media outlets, low salaries, delayed payments, insecure jobs, the growing preference for overseas education, and stronger demand for subjects perceived to offer clearer career paths.

“Most students who come to us for counselling ask which subject would be best if they want to go abroad,” said Acharya. “Out of 1,000 students, perhaps only one shows interest in journalism.”

For many students, the attraction of foreign education is reinforced by the perception that journalism offers few secure career opportunities at home. The wider media industry has struggled to create stable jobs and decent working conditions.

“Journalism itself is in a problematic state,” said Rishikesh Dahal, an associate professor at TU’s Department of Journalism and Mass Communication. “Many media outlets have disappeared and there is no longer the competition we saw before. It is natural for students to turn away from such an uncertain profession.”

According to Dahal, the media sector is struggling not only with a shrinking business model, but also with a severe erosion of public trust. "The 2015 earthquake served as an early warning for the media industry, but we failed to prepare, and the Covid pandemic subsequently hit us hard," he said.

The economic difficulties have also changed how journalists work and how audiences consume news. Social media has made publishing and distributing information easier than ever, while weakening the traditional boundaries between journalism, commentary, entertainment and influence.

Nepal’s media sector came under severe pressure during the Covid pandemic, while the September 2025 Gen Z protests brought further destruction. Journalists were injured and several newsrooms were attacked or burned during the unrest.

Dipesh Acharya, proprietor of the College of Journalism and Mass Communication (CJMC), however, argues that this should strengthen rather than weaken the case for professional journalism.

“Access to information has expanded greatly, but misleading information and clickbait content have also increased,” he said. “In such a situation, the role of professional journalism is even more important. But we need to create an environment in which the new generation entering the field can stay.”

The challenge, educators say, is that journalism education has not kept pace with changes in the industry.

Manju Mishra, founding principal of CJMC, said social media and new technology had transformed the way information was produced and distributed, but universities and journalism programmes had not adapted at the same speed.

“There is a wide gap between what is taught in classrooms and what happens in real newsrooms,” said Mishra. “Without regular internships, newsroom-based practice and access to modern communication tools, it is difficult to make journalism education relevant and market-oriented.”

Gurung agrees that the curriculum needs a major overhaul. “We need to ask what kind of curriculum we are teaching,” he said. “Is the course suited to the times, or are we still following an old syllabus? A market-oriented and contemporary curriculum is essential.”

In his experience, students are increasingly more interested in content creation than traditional journalism. That shift, he said, should not simply be treated as a threat. Journalism education could use it to teach students how to report, verify and distribute credible information across multiple platforms.

“Journalism is not just an academic subject,” said Gurung. “It produces skilled people who protect citizens’ right to information, uphold accountability and keep public debate alive.”

The history of journalism education in Nepal is much older than today’s digital media landscape. The institutional development of Nepali journalism is generally traced to the publication of Sudha Sagar in 1898 and Gorkhapatra in 1901. Formal academic journalism education began later at Ratna Rajya Laxmi Campus, where journalism was introduced at certificate level in 1976. Bachelor’s-level study followed in 1981 and master’s-level study in 2001.

Prateek Pradhan, editor-in-chief of news website Baahrakhari, said the weakness of media institutions themselves was partly responsible for the declining appeal of journalism as a career. “Media organisations have not been able to properly operate financially, so they could not pay salaries on time,” said Pradhan. “As a result, the idea has grown that perhaps one should not study journalism.”

He also warned that the public image of journalism suffers when people without a clear understanding of professional ethics become prominent through social media.

“If people can do whatever they want without understanding journalism’s principles and values, and those people gain prominence, it discourages students from studying journalism,” he said. “There has been little effort to say that journalism is worth studying or that journalism must be kept alive.”

On paper, Nepal is doing better than most of its neighbours. In practice, the space for journalism is tightening.

As the world marked World Press Freedom Day on May 3, Nepal’s position in the latest World Press Freedom Index 2026 offered a measure of reassurance. Published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), the index places Nepal 87th out of 180 countries, the highest in South Asia.

“Journalism must not die, especially at a time when democracy is under pressure globally,” said Gurung. “It is not dead. I would rather say it is changing. We need a multidisciplinary approach that matches the times and responds to what the market needs.”

articles.title: Landslide survivors spend week at health post as relief remains stalled
articles.summary:
Duk Pun Magar, 54, of Kotalbara in Thawang Rural Municipality-5, lost his home and a family member to a landslide on August 13. Since then, he has been spending his nights at a nearby health post.

“I was involved in the rescue efforts in the aftermath of the landslide,” he said. “Since I had no home to return to, I have been living here.”

Eight days after the devastating landslide killed 13 people in Kotalbara, displaced families are still spending nights at a local health post while relief supplies meant for them remain stalled along a blocked road.

Multiple landslides have blocked the road to the health post at dozens of places, leaving food, clothes and other essentials at Mabang, Pobang and Phuliban.

Buddhi Gharti Magar, chairman of Thawang-5, says the road is unlikely to reopen soon, and moving the supplies by foot would require around 200 porters.

“None of the relief materials collected in the survivors’ names has reached here,” he said. “A lot of the supplies are heaped up along the way. The ward office and villagers have been trying to make up for the shortfall.”

The immediate needs of survivors have so far been met through food and other materials provided by the local unit, its residents and survivors’ relatives. Relief brought to Kotalbara by a joint effort of the rural municipality and the Nepal Red Cross Society has been exhausted.

Local representatives have complained about poor coordination among relief providers. Individuals and organisations have been collecting aid without informing the ward office in advance, making it difficult to know what is coming and what is needed.

“We ask the relief providers to give us a list of the materials they have collected,” said Gharti Magar. “But we do not have complete information about those collecting relief. If we were informed beforehand, we could coordinate with the local administration.”

The district administration has instructed relief organisations to follow a one-door system to prevent duplication and ensure that assistance reaches genuine survivors. Assistant Chief District Officer Ghanashyam Gautam said the administration is monitoring implementation and had instructed the district road infrastructure office to clear blocked sections.

“The aim is to prevent duplication in relief collection and distribution, ensure that genuine survivors receive what they need and make proper use of the assistance received,” said Gautam. “We have also instructed the road infrastructure office to open the blocked road.”

The administration has also asked all organisations involved in relief collection and distribution to submit details of aid collected and distributed.

Survivors, however, complain that official support has been inadequate.

‘There is no other alternative to the health post,” Mek Bahadur Roka, who is taking refuge at the health post, said. “Our residential house collapsed in the landslide, and now it is difficult for us to live here without adequate support.”

With his secondary house also at extreme risk from the landslide, Roka has appealed to the government to build houses in a safe location for those in distress.

Ten displaced families, comprising 76 people, are currently affected in Kotalbara. Some houses were destroyed, and others have become unsafe to reside in. As a result, 15 to 20 people from six or seven families have been sleeping at the health post. The numbers have been fluctuating as families move out when other families offer them refuge.

Health post in-charge Nim Subedi said the facility had opened its rooms, including office space, to displaced people at night. “We have been helping displaced families spend the night in rooms at the health institution,” said Subedi. “Even after so many days since the landslide, apart from efforts at the local level, there appears to have been little effort to provide relief and shelter or reopen the road.”

According to ward officials, rice is being bought from local shops and distributed to each affected family. Residents of neighbouring Upper Uwa and other villages have also been providing vegetables.

Meanwhile, survivors have no alternative to the health post.

“It is impossible to go elsewhere during the rainy season,” Norsang Gharti Magar, another survivor taking shelter at the health post, said. “We will stay here during the monsoon and think about the future later.”

articles.title: Why we should protect Nepal’s pluralism from opportunists
articles.summary:
In Nepali politics, principles have often been traded as cheap currency. Still, the recent spectacle of Sher Bahadur Deuba, former prime minister and immediate past president of the Nepali Congress, executing a theological about-face is particularly disquieting. Having spent his years at the helm of the grand old party actively suppressing the Mahasamiti’s fervour for a return to a Hindu state, Deuba has abruptly emerged as its champion. Upon his return from East Asia amidst money-laundering investigations and Congress’s leadership change, he unceremoniously ordered his faction’s national gathering to endorse the very agenda he previously blocked repeatedly.

This is a political manoeuvre of a displaced leader attempting to establish relevance.

To understand the utter hypocrisy of this pivot, examine Deuba’s own record. During the constitutional debates of 2015, and as recently as the Mahasamiti meetings of 2018 and 2024, Deuba rejected petitions to depart from constitutional secularism signed by hundreds of party members. In his years of power, Deuba repeatedly warned that such reversal of secularism would invite division in society. Now, unseated by a special general convention and pursued by legal scrutiny, he weaponises religion as a shield. He is neither alone nor the first to indulge in this brand of opportunism. Senior politicians have historically used religious cards to keep their business afloat at the expense of festering divisions in society.

The Congress’s deposed leader is better off accepting that the separation of religion from governance is the very bedrock of civic peace. If he is looking for reasoning to change his current stance, he could turn to Jean-Jacques Rousseau, who argued that religions inevitably divide a citizen’s loyalty, as one cannot fully commit to the laws of the state whilst caught between secular duties and the decrees of a religion. If Deuba needs further logic, he could dig up Immanuel Kant’s argument that when a government uses religious doctrines to enforce laws, it treats its citizens like children, demanding obedience through divine fear rather than respecting them as rational, autonomous adults capable of moral choices. By mixing the spiritual with the political, Deuba has infantilised the Nepali populace, reducing a complex, pluralistic republic to a congregation.

The real-world consequences of this ideological regression are already visible in regional friction. Pushing a pro-Hindu political agenda systematically alienates Nepal’s significant religious and ethnic minorities—Buddhists, Muslims, Christians, and Kirat communities—relegating them to second-class status. We need only recall the recent communal clashes in the southern plains, where a trivial dispute over loudspeakers rapidly amplified, transforming neighbours into adversaries and prompting curfews.

Moreover, the religious shift cannot be separated from geopolitical shadows. Analysts point to the majoritarian influence of religion-based politics in neighbouring states, where the mainstreaming of religious nationalism has led to systemic polarisation. This model has bled across borders, emboldening Nepal’s own regressive groups. By copying this majoritarian pattern, Nepal risks inviting the structural decay seen elsewhere in the region—from the Buddhist nationalism in Sri Lanka’s civil war to the Rohingya crisis in Myanmar.

Politics is the art of compromise and pragmatism. Religion deals in the absolute. When the absolute is dragged into the mud of political factionalism, both are corrupted. In Nepal’s context, secularism was one of the hardest-won compromises of a decade-long civil war that dismantled a feudal Hindu monarchy to build an inclusive republic. It cannot be sacrificed on the altar of one man’s desperate quest for political survival. If Deuba’s faction succeeds in dragging the Congress down this sectarian path, they will set fire to Nepal’s constitutional foundations.

Nepal’s future lies in looking forward, not backwards. The gods do not belong in the realm of politics. Deuba might succeed in commanding the support of regressive religious groups with his ideological pivot, but his deliberate divine deception must be rejected by both the public and his faction’s cadres.

articles.title: Time to introduce charter schools in Nepal?
articles.summary:
Nepal’s public education system has been in shambles for a long time due to political instability and poor governance, as documented in a collection of research papers published by Martin Chautari, School Education in Nepal (2021). Recent directives issued by the Minister of Education and Sports, Sasmit Pokharel, are attempts to alter course. The current government might indeed be equipped to make sweeping changes due to its historic mandate. Following one of Minister Pokharel’s directives, the Curriculum Development Centre is in the process of revising the school-level National Curriculum Framework (NCF) under a task force led by the Dean of Kathmandu University’s School of Education. “The goal is not cosmetic change but systemic transformation…and the new NCF must be relevant, responsive and rigorous,” he implored at the mid-July orientation session.

Radical restructuring?

Despite good intentions, the NCF revision may not translate to actual change on the ground. Several studies, such as the report by the U4 Anti-Corruption Resource Centre—Reforming Nepal’s education system for greater integrity and improved outcomes—have pointed out glaring disconnects between policies and practice in Nepal’s education sector over the decades due to a culture of corruption, fragile monitoring systems, improper teacher management, and a general lack of trust. It might be time to introduce innovative models of school structure and governance, such as charter schools, which function on the basis of a contract between the government and a committee of stakeholders.

Funded by the government but operating with a degree of autonomy, the first charter school started in Minnesota in the United States in 1991. Since then, it has spread across the country, with each state having their own laws governing the establishment, regulation and functioning of charter schools. Similar public-private models have since been running in other developed countries like the UK, Canada and Sweden. Japan, Pakistan and Qatar also have similar models. An article published in 2016 by the National Association of Charter School Authorizers described how New Delhi was also considering ‘government partnership’ schools that would bring in private operators to run public schools.

Attempts at decentralising education

During the first half of the 20th century, most public schools in Nepal were founded and managed by local communities, and were called by different names based on differing principles and goals: English, Bhasha, Basic, Sanskrit and so on. In 1957, massive protests erupted, especially in Tarai, against the government’s directive to use Nepali as a medium of instruction in all schools. Later, the Panchayat government (1960–1990) took control of the education system, mandating “a uniform education system in the country with a single language of instruction”. Nationalising and centralising the education system in a diverse, multicultural society was like trying to put a square peg in a round hole.

After the dawn of democracy and neoliberalism in the 1990s, the private sector proliferated and public schools deteriorated. The state began a process of decentralisation in the early 2000s, but the ongoing People’s War hampered these efforts. Federalism and a demand for decentralisation were a response to the centralised bureaucracy detached and disconnected from most of the country. Although the current Constitution of Nepal explicitly grants local governments authority to manage all aspects of school education, this has been a point of contention, with teachers’ unions staging protests, wanting to be part of the cadre of the central government.

From chaos comes order

A paper published by Kuber Prasad Bhetwal in 2022, Effectiveness of Local Curriculum Implementation in Nepal, has a list of findings and suggestions from his field study in Sankhuwasaba’s primary schools. Most interviewed teachers supported teaching local curricula that include local issues. Charter schools could similarly be founded with goals and visions that suit local culture, language and needs. But the paper also identifies that building new curricula and systems is hampered by a lack of human resources. Sankhuwasaba’s district administrative personnel had minimal experience with local curriculum development and implementation.

Given Nepal’s multilingual, multiethnic reality, provincial and local governments are best positioned to deliver education. They should be supported to design unique charter schools and hire and train experts who are more responsive to and knowledgeable about local issues. Perhaps a radical systemic restructuring will be a worthy experiment, although we have to be wary of commercial interests, especially in the delivery of public services. There is already widespread discontent regarding a lack of proper regulation of profit-seeking private schools. But I’m simply offering an option out of the quagmire that has been Nepal’s public education system.

We must consider alternatives suitable for a diverse populace. Charter schools won’t be perfect, but a massive overhaul will create opportunities to tap into young talents and mobilise them across the country—similar to how Teach for Nepal has been functioning. Since we already have three tiers of government, and the Federal Education Act has still not been passed, this might be a moment to truly imagine a new system that could work with the local and provincial governments to deliver educational services effectively and efficiently. It will undoubtedly be extremely challenging to imagine and implement large-scale changes. But if the government is indeed serious about improving public services and creating a long-lasting impact, it should take bold, radical steps and make arrangements accordingly.

articles.title: It takes a global village
articles.summary:
Nepal has roughly $53 billion sitting in bank deposits. Around $14 billion enters the country each year through remittances. Its technology sector is now estimated to export more than $1 billion in services. Yet, promising Nepali enterprises still struggle to find the capital, capabilities and markets they need to scale.

That paradox has become harder to ignore as traditional development finance contracts. Official development assistance fell by 23 percent globally in 2025, its largest annual contraction on record, with a further decline projected in 2026. Nepal is simultaneously preparing to graduate from the Least Developed Country status, even as AI rapidly reshapes economies, organisations and the capabilities they need.

Perhaps, then, the question is not only what Nepal lacks. It is why so much of what we already have remains difficult to connect, mobilise and scale.

For me, that question became personal over the past year. After nearly two decades in international development, including more than a decade at USAID, I found myself reconsidering some of the assumptions that had shaped my own career: what was worth carrying forward, what needed to change, and where institutions like ours could add distinctive value.

Over the year, our team worked across all seven provinces and encountered the same paradox.

Entrepreneurs were looking for investors; investors for investment-ready enterprises. Universities were producing graduates; employers were struggling to find the capabilities they needed. Researchers were generating useful evidence, but practitioners often struggled to find, translate or apply it. Development organisations were piloting solutions; businesses with the technology, networks or commercial incentives to help them scale were often not in the same room. More than a shortage of effort, ideas or resources, the constraint was the pathways between them.

We talk a great deal about physical infrastructure in Nepal, and rightly so. But economies also depend on intangible infrastructure: trust, relationships, shared knowledge, credible intermediaries and networks that allow capital, talent and ideas to find one another—and promising solutions to scale.

For instance, $7,200 from FCDO’s Nepal in Business-Growth Advisors programme funded an investment-readiness initiative that we delivered for Nepali technology companies. One participant, Raindrop, went on to secure a strategic partner who brings deep expertise as well as investment of approximately $131,000—more than 18 times that initial investment.

Consider the wider capital landscape: roughly $53 billion in bank deposits, $39 billion in lending, and around $14 billion in annual remittances, compared with a federal capital budget of about $14 billion and roughly $400 million in foreign grants. Capital and opportunity exist, but the structures, information, incentives and trust that allow them to meet often do not.

When grants can no longer be assumed—or sustained at familiar scale—what other assets do organisations have to work with? Quite a lot: community trust; deep local networks; institutional knowledge of what localisation, inclusion and equity require in practice; relationships across sectors; data; convening power; and implementation capability.

These assets have economic value too. Private capital cannot replace public or philanthropic resources where markets cannot or will not go.
